facts.fact: A script that raises still leaves Blender's exit code at 0 unless --python-exit-code is given
sys.exit(N) inside a --python script ends Blender with exit code N
Through a pipe, which ways of printing reach the reader while the script still runs (a 3 s pause between two lines; True = the first line arrived before the pause ended)
sys.argv inside Blender holds Blender's own arguments too; a script's own arguments are the ones after '--', and Blender does not act on them
Starting headless Blender, running an empty script and quitting takes about this long (3 runs each)
A driver whose expression needs Python stays unevaluated in a file opened headless unless autoexec is on (-y); a simple expression such as 'frame * 2' is evaluated either way
Command-line arguments run in order: --python-expr placed before -f changed the scene before the frame rendered (the PNG came out at the script's size)
'-- --cycles-device METAL' changes the device used without changing scene.cycles.device; timed on the factory cube at 320 px with 512 samples, adaptive sampling off

In background mode bpy.context has a window and screen (from the opened file) but no area, region or space; the scene, view layer and active object are the file's; operators that need a 3D view or a screen area fail their poll, while object, mesh and edit-mode operators work
